name: Verbesina

project_scope.selection_mode: Current canonical manifest: three learner species in Verbesina; preserve original inclusion/range states
project_scope.notes: This is a field teaching subset of Verbesina in Central Texas, not a worldwide genus key. Additional lookalikes Verbesina alternifolia occur elsewhere but are not canonical here.

priority: actual winter ice ribbons separately from flowers
pappus awns as final microscopic verification
study_strategy.warning: Frostweed is Verbesina virginica; it is not a genus that blooms with ice. Winged stems also occur in V. alternifolia, whose flowers are yellow.

look_here_first: FIRST find the flower color and STEM WINGS. White heads in a tall MANY-HEAD fall canopy + obvious long decurrent green stem wings → frostweed, V. virginica. YELLOW heads: if ONE HUGE yellow head on a short PERENNIAL with mostly OPPOSITE leaves and NO wings → Lindheimer's crownbeard. If a branching gray-hairy ANNUAL with TRIANGULAR leaves and yellow daisy heads, without obvious winged internodes → cowpen daisy, V. encelioides. For any uncertain plant, check head number/size and mid-stem phyllotaxy before using habitat.
shared_genus_traits: Sunflower-family (Asteraceae) taxa with capitula (flower heads) made of ray florets around disc florets; a 'flower head' is a cluster of true florets.
Leaves usually opposite or alternate depending on species and position; juvenile/lower leaves may have different arrangement from upper leaves.
Fruits are flattened cypselae, sometimes with papery wings; pappus awns vary by species and are NOT the same as winged stems.
Stem wings are species-dependent. Winged green stems support frostweed but do not define all Verbesina; V. alternifolia is another wingstem lookalike.
Autumn composites often need plant habit, stem features, leaf arrangement and individual capitulum size together—not flower color alone.

species_comparison_matrix.virginica: WHITE or cream: very many tiny composite heads, each typically 1–3(–5) short white rays and 8–13 disc florets
species_comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: YELLOW: large often solitary capitulum with about 13 LONG yellow rays and 80–120 disc florets
species_comparison_matrix.encelioides: YELLOW: several larger showy daisy heads with ~12–15 yellow rays, 80–150 disc florets

species_comparison_matrix.virginica: Broad, wavily decurrent green stem wings from leaf bases; inspect healthy green internodes
Mainly ALTERNATE; large rough elongate leaves, bases taper and descend as wings, edges toothed to nearly entire
species_comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: Mostly OPPOSITE; smaller ovate to deltate leaves, bases rounded/cuneate, teeth variable
species_comparison_matrix.encelioides: Upper ALTERNATE but lower may be opposite; triangular/ovate gray-green coarse-toothed leaves

species_comparison_matrix.virginica: Robust herbaceous perennial, often 1–2+ m; domed/panicled white canopy
species_comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: Shorter perennial ~0.3–0.7 m, single prominent yellow head
species_comparison_matrix.encelioides: Annual, branching weed, often 0.1–1.2 m; swales, disturbed sites

species_comparison_matrix.virginica: Flattened WINGED cypsela with TWO persistent AWNS 1.5–3 mm
species_comparison_matrix.lindheimeri: Dark ~7 mm fruit, tiny/absent awns ~0–0.5 mm
species_comparison_matrix.encelioides: Flattened narrow obovate 3.5–5+ mm fruit with shorter awns 0.5–1+ mm (ray fruits may lack awns)

quick_key.if: Many little white flower heads on tall perennial with green, wavy, vertically WINGED internodes
Big yellow solitary (sometimes few) flower head, mostly opposite leaves, no winged stem, low limestone perennial
Several larger yellow composite heads on branching annual, triangular grayish hairy leaves, upper alternate leaves, no winged stem
Tall winged stems like frostweed but YELLOW flower heads
quick_key.then: Check Verbesina alternifolia (wingstem) and other taxa — outside the current canonical three

comparison_cards.title: Frostweed vs Lindheimer's crownbeard — color PLUS stem anatomy
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Look at the STEM: broad decurrent leafy wings = frostweed; Lindheimer's is unwinged. Then check a WHOLE head cluster: many white tiny heads in frostweed versus one or a few large yellow heads in Lindheimer's. Leaves are usually alternate vs mostly opposite.

field_matrix.virginica: Obvious thin wing flanges descending from leaves
Usually alternate, large rough, tapering decurrent base

comparison_cards.caution: No single feature is equally obvious throughout the year. Old basal frostweed stems may lose green wing tissue; check leafy mid-stem internodes.

comparison_cards.title: Frostweed vs cowpen daisy — don't confuse composites
comparison_cards.look_here_first: The color/head scale is immediate: frostweed is many tiny WHITE heads, cowpen is fewer much BIGGER YELLOW daisy heads. Mid-stem frostweed wings vs non-winged cowpen, then coarse triangular cowpen leaves help before flowering.

field_matrix.virginica: Many tiny whitish heads each with 1–3 short white ray florets
field_matrix.encelioides: Larger showy yellow heads each with 12–15+ long yellow rays

field_matrix.virginica: Leaf bases extend down as conspicuous vertical wings
Elongate rough leaves, mostly alternate and decurrent
field_matrix.encelioides: Triangle/ovate often gray-hairy blades, coarse marginal teeth; lower can be opposite
Annual often on disturbed exposed ground

comparison_cards.title: What exactly is a frost flower?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Inspect the BASE OF THE STEM just after suitable subfreezing temperatures: sheets of ice curl and push out of fissures when water emerges and freezes. It is not a corolla, not a seed, and not guaranteed every freezing night.

Frostweed green leaves and flowering head appear fall
field_matrix.ice: Ice ribbons occur on some freezing winter mornings and melt quickly

field_matrix.plant: Confirm winged stem and white flowering head during growing season
field_matrix.ice: Other species can make similar frost flowers; no ice is a non-test

visual_comparison.subtitle: Real exact-species CC photos for frostweed and cowpen daisy. The crispest exact stem-wing macro remains an educational link to UT Austin because reuse rights are unknown. Lindheimer's licensed matched photo remains a final polish goal.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Frostweed = WINGED green stem + 60–100 TINY WHITE heads + seasonal ice ribbons. Yellow big solitary = Lindheimer's. Yellow big several = cowpen daisy.
